extracted.intended_audience: State Exchanges, Federal Exchange operators (HealthCare.gov), QHP issuers, agents/brokers/web-brokers, and other stakeholders affected by HHS Marketplace rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the proposed regulatory requirements, information-collection requirements (ICRs), and operational standards in the HHS proposed rule affecting Exchanges, agents/brokers/web-brokers, and QHP issuers. Includes who must do what, verification/eligibility rules, data/reporting obligations, and estimated burdens/costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of HHS-approved consumer consent form
rubrics_metrics.description: Require agents, brokers, and web-brokers to use the HHS-approved and -created consumer consent form to meet the eligibility application review documentation requirements and the consumer consent documentation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form may be submitted electronically (so no printing/mailing costs). HHS would include this as a new information collection for OMB review if finalized. OMB burden/cost estimates and public comment are being solicited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on misleading marketing (§155.220(j)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendments to §155.220(j) creating new standards of conduct on marketing requirements to prohibit agents, brokers, and web-brokers from engaging in misleading marketing, and to require provision of marketing materials to HHS upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New regulations housed in §155.220(j)(3) must be adhered to, including requirements in §155.220(j)(3)(iii). HHS may request advertisements (§155.220(j)(3)(iv)). Enforcement notifications are expected to be ~70 annually: ~2/3 as Technical Assistance (TA) requiring only confirmation removal, ~1/3 as Notices of Intent to Terminate (NoITs) requiring confirmation of ad removal and review of CMS marketing guidelines. HHS estimates ~24 notifications annually that require documentation; estimated response time ~1 hour per notification. Responding entities must remove noncompliant ads and/or review marketing guidelines and respond by email; HHS provides hyperlinks to noncompliant ads. HHS seeks comment on burden estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBE-EDE Blueprint revision requirement (§155.221)
rubrics_metrics.description: State Exchanges that elect to implement the State-Based Exchange Enhanced Direct Enrollment (SBE-EDE) option must revise their Exchange Blueprint to notify HHS that the State proposes to implement SBE-EDE in compliance with related requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions are made by logging into the CMS web interface repository for Exchange Blueprints. Burden expected to be nominal; the collection is currently covered under OMB Control Number 0938-1172. HHS seeks comment on burden associated with this activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and alignment of 'eligible noncitizen' (45 CFR 155.20; 42 CFR 600.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add new definition of 'eligible noncitizen' at 45 CFR 155.20 and for BHP at 42 CFR 600.5, and update §155.305(f)(1)(ii) to align APTC eligibility rules so Exchanges grant eligibility for APTC only to individuals defined as 'U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, and eligible noncitizens' provided other APTC requirements are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change becomes effective beginning PY 2027 and applies to Federal platform Exchanges, the 22 State Exchanges expected in PY 2027, and BHP-operating States. Exchanges must update eligibility/enrollment systems to collect applicant attestations regarding eligible noncitizen status, determine whether attestations can be verified, set/process new inconsistencies where attestations cannot be verified, and ensure current enrollees who become ineligible have APTC and CSR eligibility ended accordingly. HHS seeks comment; implementation will be submitted for OMB review (0938-NEW for Exchanges and 0938-1218 for BHP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Data Services Hub Verify Lawful Presence (VLP) updates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Data Services Hub must be updated to enable Exchanges to accurately verify whether an individual is an eligible noncitizen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS estimates the Hub will need ~2,000 hours in 2025: 500 hours for a database/network admin & architect at $103.34/hr and 1,500 hours for a computer programmer at $94.88/hr, totaling ~$193,990 in one-time 2025 burden. Exchanges on the Federal platform and State Exchanges also face one-time technical update burdens (estimates provided elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: One-time technical update requirements and cost estimates for Exchanges and States
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges on the Federal platform and State Exchanges must make one-time system updates in specified staffing categories (database/network admin & architect; computer programmer) to implement eligibility and verification changes (e.g., eligible noncitizen verification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS provides detailed hour and wage estimates: e.g., Exchanges on the Federal platform estimated 7,000 hours (1,750 hrs admin @ $103.34 + 5,250 hrs programmer @ $94.88) = $678,965; similar per-State estimates multiplied by number of State Exchanges. These are presented as estimated one-time burdens/costs for implementation in 2025/2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of new DMI type for 'eligible noncitizens' (ongoing burden expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creation of a new Data Matching Issue (DMI) type for 'eligible noncitizens' is proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS anticipates this proposed policy would not result in ongoing burden changes for Exchanges and individuals related to the creation of a new DMI type because these individuals would already be required to submit documentation to verify eligibility to enroll in a QHP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of APTC for certain noncitizens with income below 100% FPL (§155.305(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to disallow APTC for coverage of noncitizens who are ineligible for Medicaid due to immigration status and have income below 100% of the FPL; Exchanges must implement related eligibility system updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS estimates one-time technical update hours for Exchanges on Federal platform (2,500 hours) and each State Exchange (2,000 hours) with detailed staffing breakdowns and cost estimates. The rule discussion includes estimates of DMI reductions and ongoing burden changes resulting from this and related policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existing verification practice: require documentation when trusted data cannot verify attestation
rubrics_metrics.description: Current Exchange practice: when an applicant attests to information (e.g., lawful presence or income) and trusted data sources cannot promptly verify that attestation, Exchanges must require individuals to submit documentation to verify their attested application information (generates DMIs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the baseline operational standard referenced across multiple proposed changes; HHS provides time-per-verification estimates (commonly 1.2 hours for eligibility support staff) and cost calculations for reductions or increases in DMIs resulting from policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1-tax year Failure To File and Reconcile (FTR) process (§155.305(f)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend §155.305(f)(4) so that in PY 2028 and beyond, Exchanges may not determine an individual eligible for APTC if HHS notifies the Exchange that APTC were paid for a year and the tax filer did not file a Federal income tax return and reconcile APTC for that year (the '1-tax year FTR' process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchanges may implement this earlier (PY 2027) at their option if capable. Exchanges on the Federal platform intend to adopt the 1-year FTR in PY 2027. Minimal changes to Exchange application questions for HealthCare.gov are anticipated; HHS does not expect significant PRA impacts related to noticing requirements. HHS seeks comment on burden/assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income verification when trusted data indicate income <100% FPL (§155.320(c)(3)(iii)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: Update §155.320(c)(3)(iii)(A) to extend requirement for applicants to submit documentation when their attested household income is within the APTC range but trusted data sources indicate income less than 100% of the FPL; implement as a new permanent verification process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS estimates consumer burden ~1 hour per inconsistency, with historical estimates of ~340,000 household-level inconsistencies on the Federal platform and ~208,000 on State Exchanges (total ~548,000 hours consumer burden annually). Exchange processing estimated at 1.2 hours per verification at $49.52/hr, with detailed annual cost estimates. One-time system expenses in 2026 for eligibility system updates are estimated (8,000 hours per entity with staff breakdowns and costs). HHS seeks comment on burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of §155.320(c)(5) — income verification when tax data unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove §155.320(c)(5), eliminating the allowance that would let Exchanges continue the income verification process when IRS is contacted but returns no data rather than accepting applicant attestation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change, implemented as a permanent verification procedure, is estimated to generate very large numbers of inconsistencies (e.g., 1,722,000 household-level for Federal platform, 1,056,000 for State Exchanges), with per-verification Exchange work estimated at 1.2 hours and consumer time ~1 hour per submission. HHS estimates significant annual increases in hours and monetary burden, plus one-time system-update costs for 2026 (9,000 hours per entity with staff breakdowns). HHS seeks comment on these estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-enrollment SEP verification requirements (§155.420(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow the Federal Exchange to conduct pre-enrollment verification for SEPs other than Loss of Minimum Essential Coverage and require Exchanges on the Federal Platform to conduct pre-enrollment verification for at least 75 percent of new enrollments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS estimates consumer time ~1 hour per verification; historical FFE data suggests ~293,073 new SEP verification issues annually on the Federal platform, increasing consumer burden ~293,073 hours and Exchange burden ~58,615 hours (0.2 hours per verification) at $49.52/hr. HHS seeks comment on burden estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expansion of hardship exemption eligibility (§155.605(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals ineligible for APTC or CSRs due to projected household income may apply for a hardship exemption to qualify for catastrophic coverage; the FFE automatically grants these exemptions through the application system when consumers apply for catastrophic coverage, but some consumers may submit paper applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper application consumer burden ~16 minutes; manual review by Exchange staff (four State Exchanges that process their own exemptions) ~19 minutes per application at $49.52/hr, yielding a per-application processing cost estimate of $15.75. HHS estimates ~1,072 applications annually for the four State Exchanges with a total annual cost ~$16,884. If States adopt automated processing (like FFE) or delegate processing to HHS, manual processing burden could be eliminated. HHS seeks comment and notes variability by State enrollment volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of Exchange Network Adequacy Standards (§155.1050)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to amend §155.1050(a)(2) to remove the requirement (for plan years beginning Jan 1, 2027) that State Exchanges and SBE-FPs establish and impose quantitative time and distance network adequacy standards at least as stringent as FFE standards under §156.230 and to eliminate the prior requirement to conduct quantitative network adequacy reviews before certifying a QHP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead, require State Exchanges and SBE-FPs to ensure each QHP provides sufficient access to providers meeting the applicable standards (§156.230(a)(1)(ii)/(a)(1)(iii) for network plans or proposed §156.236(a) for non-network plans). HHS recognizes many States have robust standards and will continue to evaluate local market conditions. HHS estimates minimal increased issuer burden and provides prior estimated burdens for network adequacy review (up to 900 hours per State Exchange/SBE-FP at $75.40/hr = $67,860/year). HHS seeks comment on burden estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of duplication between SEIPM and annual independent external programmatic audits (§155.1200)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend §155.1200(d) to reduce duplication between the proposed SEIPM program (subpart Q) and annual independent external programmatic audit requirements; add §155.1200(e) to permit a State Exchange to satisfy certain annual audit requirements by completing the SEIPM process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS projects a programmatic audit cost reduction of approximately $45,000 annually per State Exchange (based on average external audit cost of $150,000), totaling ~$990,000 across 22 State Exchanges, beginning as early as 2027. This change also introduces a new burden associated with completing the SEIPM process; HHS seeks comment and feedback from State Exchanges on audit cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEIPM reporting and data submission requirements (§155.1615)
rubrics_metrics.description: State Exchanges participating in SEIPM must provide to HHS: (a) Program Information (policy, operational and technical documentation including business rules, calculations, entity relationships, data dictionaries, operating procedures, and system technology) and (b) the universe of tax household information for the plan year under review (listing of tax households enrolled in a QHP with identifiers, QHP policy identifiers within tax household, tax household size, total payment amounts for each sampled unit for the benefit year, and info about existence of eligibility verification inconsistencies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Information is retained in digital format and can be electronically transmitted; HHS estimates the burden for collection and transfer of this Program Information would be no more than 40 hours. The burden for providing the universe of tax household information includes the time for State Exchanges to meet with HHS to review submitted information. HHS seeks comment on burden estimates and assumptions.
